en: A militant yakuza once feared as the Mad Dog of Shimano. He strove to rebuild the clan after quitting his lieutenant post to assume an advisory role a few years ago, but was unhappy with the new generation's focus on making money rather than fighting. After Saejima's return, he was reminded of the need for strong, old-school yakuza, and together they pledged to support Daigo. He is serving as Daigo's right-hand man while Saejima does time before becoming captain.

A militant yakuza once feared as the Mad Dog of Shimano. He strove to rebuild the clan after quitting his lieutenant post to assume an advisory role a few years ago, but was unhappy with the new generation's focus on making money rather than fighting. After Saejima's return, he was reminded of the need for strong, old-school yakuza, and together they pledged to support Daigo. He is serving as Daigo's right-hand man while Saejima does time before becoming captain. To bring local families into the fold before war with the Omi, he went to Sapporo for talks with the Kitakata, where he was subsequently murdered.

A detective who has built up a rapport with Kiryu and the others, after working together in the ten billion yen incident. He handed in his badge for a time and worked as a newspaper reporter focusing on politics, but now he's back on the force. He continues to have a good relationship with the mama of New Serena.

Owner of the New Serena lounge in Kamurocho. Date helped her out when she started her business, so she always gives special treatment to Kiryu and the others. She was once married to a policeman, but he was killed in the line of duty. She fears the same could happen to Date and avoided getting involved with him as more than a customer, but in the last few years they've grown close.

An inmate who shares a room with Saejima. He is easygoing, and has a knack for cheering up his cellmates. Though not affiliated with yakuza, he calls Saejima "boss." It's not clear what he's in for, but it doesn't sound like he'll do too much time.

An inmate who shares a room with Saejima. He is easygoing, and has a knack for cheering up his cellmates. Though not affiliated with yakuza, he calls Saejima "boss." He used to be a homicide detective, but was dismissed and imprisoned on corruption charges. He kept his past a secret for fear that other prisoners would hold a grudge against him. Using a guard's revolver, he shot down Kugihara to save Saejima.
An inmate who shares a room with Saejima, and the oldest of the bunch. Not a lot gets past him, and after he spotted that Saejima was injured, he somehow managed to procure painkillers for him.

An inmate who shares a room with Saejima, and the oldest of the bunch. Not a lot gets past him, and after he spotted that Saejima was injured, he somehow managed to procure painkillers for him. A legendary larcenist who pulled off over 15,000 thefts without getting caught, he turned himself in at the age of 60. It seems he did a little work as a doctor in his youth, and he used these skills to patch up Kosaka after Kugihara stabbed him.

An inmate who shares a room with Saejima. The youngest among the cellmates, he was transferred to Abashiri just a year ago. He looks up to Saejima as an older brother. He has already spent over ten years in prison, with more to serve in his long sentence. He belonged to a yakuza group in Hokkaido, but was jailed after committing murder on behalf of a senior member. Since then none of his former buddies have been in touch, and he now realizes he was used. He fears going back into the real world and abandoned his parole application.

An inmate who shared a cell with Saejima. He treated Saejima like an older brother, but all the stories about his past were lies. He was really sent to Abashiri to monitor Saejima and make sure he came to Tsukimino at the right time, using Kugihara to control the timing of his release. However, he had a change of heart after Saejima saved his life and felt guilty for his betrayal. He tried to commit suicide, but was stopped by Saejima. After losing a fight with Saejima, he disappears.

A prisoner who came to Abashiri about six months ago. He leads the woodworking crew, and has many other prisoners on his side. For some reason he is targeting Saejima, luring him to secluded storerooms and beating him to a pulp during exercise periods.

A prisoner who came to Abashiri about six months ago. He leads the woodworking crew, and has many other prisoners on his side. He was targeting Saejima, luring him to secluded storerooms and beating him to a pulp during exercise periods. His motive was to provoke Saejima into fighting him, so his sentence would be extended. Under the original plan he was to start a riot so that Saejima could get away easier, but his hatred drove him to try to kill Saejima instead. Before he could do that, he was shot in the chest by Himura.

A strict disciplinarian who punishes any breach of the rules, he has been known to revoke parole and extend sentences for the most minor infractions. He had his eye on Saejima as a potential troublemaker, and in response to Kugihara's harassment of Saejima, he put Saejima in solitary confinement.

A strict disciplinarian who punishes any breach of the rules, he has been known to revoke parole and extend sentences for the most minor infractions. He had his eye on Saejima as a potential troublemaker, but after he was expelled from the Tojo Clan, he slowly starts to sympathize. After the warden is attacked and Kugihara calls in a large number of prisoners, he sees trouble on the horizon and decides to help Saejima escape. He was stabbed by Kugihara, but survived thanks to Oshima's first aid.
A hunter who lives in a small mountain village. He saved a stranded Saejima, and looked after him at his house. A man of few words, he hasn't opened up to the other villagers and is seen as a loner.

A hunter who lives in a small mountain village. He saved a stranded Saejima, and looked after him at his house. A man of few words, he hasn't opened up to the other villagers and is seen as a loner. After Saejima saved Baba and talked of leaving, Okudera spoke to him about the difference between necessary and unnecessary killing, saying revenge solves nothing.

Patriarch of the Kitakata Family, a yakuza group that controls Hokkaido's largest entertainment district, Tsukimino. He rules over the hawkers in the area, running events like the Snow Festival. He has close ties with his community and doesn't demand protection money, making him popular. He was approached about an alliance with the Tojo Clan by Goro Majima, but Majima was killed in Sapporo during these talks, making Kitakata a prime suspect.

Patriarch of the Kitakata Family, a yakuza group that controls Hokkaido's largest entertainment district, Tsukimino. He rules over the hawkers in the area, running events like the Snow Festival. He has close ties with his community and doesn't demand protection money, making him popular. He was approached about an alliance with the Tojo Clan by Goro Majima, but Majima was killed in Sapporo during these talks, making Kitakata a prime suspect. Before revealing the truth to Saejima, he was shot by Baba and went into a coma.

A detective with the organized crime unit of the Osaka Prefectural Police. He is trying to stop the impending war between Omi and the Tojo Clan, without involving the Tokyo Metropolitan Police. To resolve the conflict without direct involvement, he talked to Kiryu in Fukuoka and stopped Morinaga from making trouble with Watase. After pointing Kiryu toward Tokyo, he appeared in Sapporo and took Saejima into custody. When Saejima hits a dead end with Kitakata, the detective talks him into heading to Tokyo.

A girl who was caught up in the ten billion yen incident. Until a year and a half ago she was living at an orphanage in Okinawa with Kazuma Kiryu, but then she was scouted by Park and moved to Osaka to break into the entertainment industry. She is currently working day and night on her vocal and dance training at Dyna Chair, with the aim of winning the Princess League competition and making her major label debut.

A girl who was caught up in the ten billion yen incident. Until a year and a half ago she was living at an orphanage in Okinawa with Kazuma Kiryu, but then she was scouted by Park and moved to Osaka to break into the entertainment industry. But when Park suddenly dies, Haruka and Akiyama decide to get to the bottom of this tragedy. After discovering Ousaka Enterprises had a hand in Park's death, and learning that Park's ex-husband Majima was alive and had planned to meet her in Tokyo, Haruka heads there to perform her debut concert and fulfill her promise to Park.

The owner of moneylender Sky Finance in Kamurocho. Known as the Lifeline of Kamurocho, he lends to those unable to get financing elsewhere. He places special conditions on loans to each customer, and only lends them cash once these conditions are met. He has been coming to Osaka a lot lately to work on opening a branch in Sotenbori.

The owner of moneylender Sky Finance in Kamurocho. Known as the Lifeline of Kamurocho, he lends to those unable to get financing elsewhere. He places special conditions on loans to each customer, and only lends them cash once these conditions are met. He had been frequenting Osaka to open a branch in Sotenbori, but after Park's death he was reunited with Haruka at Dyna Chair. Through their investigation, they discovered Ousaka Enterprises' involvement. With Haruka's life in danger, he took her to Tokyo to ensure Park's dream was fulfilled.

President of Dyna Chair Productions, situated in Sotenbori, Osaka. Though her company is small, she has an eye for talent and has earned many friends and collaborators in the industry. That said, many others dislike her aggressive way of doing things. After scouring the country for talent, she found and recruited Haruka in Okinawa. She has Haruka working day and night to prepare for her major label debut in just six months.

President of Dyna Chair Productions, situated in Sotenbori, Osaka. She was once a pop idol herself, but her dreams never came to fruition. After scouring the country for talent, she found and recruited Haruka in Okinawa. Though strict with Haruka, they formed an almost mother-daughter bond. She had arranged to see her ex-husband Majima at Haruka's debut concert, but asked Haruka to meet him instead. Before that could happen, she was killed by Ogita as he searched for Majima's letter.
Haruka's manager. A good-natured guy who treats young Haruka with genuine kindness, but can sometimes be slack in his duties. He always seems to be getting scolded by Park for his mistakes.

Haruka's manager. A good-natured guy who treats young Haruka with genuine kindness, but can sometimes be slack in his duties. After Park's sudden death, he is touched by Haruka's determination to fulfill her dream and carries on with his job. However, he is knocked off the roof of the building by Kanai, who had come to look for Majima's letter. Though he survives, he is hospitalized with serious injuries.

Haruka's vocal coach. She was once a singer herself, but now works behind the scenes. A spirited woman, she is strict with Haruka during lessons, hoping to bring her up to the level where she can make her debut.

Haruka's vocal coach. She was once a singer herself, but now works behind the scenes. After Park's sudden death, she and Horie do their best to help Haruka make her debut, and when Horie is hospitalized she takes over as Haruka's manager. When it is revealed that Park had planned a concert at Japan Dome for Haruka's debut, though intimidated, she does her best to organize the event.

A freelance dance instructor. Though he initially signed a contract with Park to get Haruka ready in a year, when the schedule is moved forward he is forced to frantically try to prepare her in six months.

A freelance dance instructor. Though he initially signed a contract with Park to get Haruka ready in a year, after the schedule was moved forward he frantically tried to prepare her in six months. However, Park terminated his contract and he was left out in the cold. Kanai of Ousaka Enterprises asked him to steal Majima's letter from Park to settle his debt, but he ended up killing her by mistake. He was also present when Kanai confronted Horie, but after failing to find the letter, Kanai ended his life.
